titulo: He hasn't got an ounce of sense
intro: Describing character precisely: the nouns for qualities, the adjectives, and a few colourful idioms.
p.tacaño.consejo: It is colloquial and a bit negative. The noun is «la tacañería».
p.cobarde.consejo: It has the same form for both genders: «un chico cobarde», «una chica cobarde».
p.valiente.consejo: Same for both genders. Its noun is «la valentía».
p.susceptible.consejo: It describes someone who is easily offended. Its noun is «la susceptibilidad».
p.constante.consejo: Its noun is «la constancia». The opposite is «inconstante».
p.timidez.consejo: It comes from «tímido» plus «-ez». The final z sounds «th» in Spain.
p.generosidad.consejo: It comes from «generoso». Nouns in «-dad» are feminine: «la generosidad».
p.valentía.consejo: It comes from «valiente». It is the opposite of «la cobardía».
p.cobardía.consejo: It comes from «cobarde». It has an accent on the «í»: «cobardía».
p.tener carácter.consejo: «Tener mal carácter» is getting angry easily; «buen carácter», getting on with everybody.
p.no tener dos dedos de frente.glosa: to have no sense at all
p.no tener dos dedos de frente.consejo: It is colloquial and harsh: use it only with people you know well.
p.estar como una cabra.consejo: It is colloquial and usually said fondly: «mi tío está como una cabra».
b1.texto:
At this level you talk about qualities as things, so you need the nouns. Each ending has its pattern:

- **-dad**: generoso → **la generosidad**; sincero → **la sinceridad**
- **-ez**: tímido → **la timidez**; maduro → **la madurez**
- **-ía**: valiente → **la valentía**; cobarde → **la cobardía**
- **-ura**: tierno → **la ternura**
- **-ismo**: egoísta → **el egoísmo**
- **-ción / -cia**: ambicioso → **la ambición**; arrogante → **la arrogancia**

**The opposite** is formed with **in-**, **im-** or **ir-**: **inconstante**, **impuntual**, **irresponsable**.

**Ser or tener.** **Es valiente** = **tiene valentía**.

**False friend.** In Spanish **sensible** is someone who feels a lot; someone who thinks wisely is **sensato**.

**Colourful idioms.** **No tiene dos dedos de frente**: he has little sense. **Está como una cabra**: he is mad, said fondly. **Es un trozo de pan**: he is very kind.
b2.f0.texto: The new boss is very ambitious.
b2.f1.texto: But he is persevering and never gives up.
b2.f2.texto: I think he is a bit mean.
b2.f3.texto: He never treats anyone to a coffee.
b2.f5.texto: The previous boss was a real sweetheart.
b2.f6.texto: But he didn't have much personality.
b2.f7.texto: You need courage to talk to him.
b4.texto:
**The noun of a quality** comes from the adjective with an ending:

- **-dad** and **-ez**: **la generosidad**, **la timidez**
- **-ía**: **la valentía**, **la cobardía**
- **-ción** and **-cia**: **la ambición**, **la arrogancia**

They are all feminine, except those ending in **-ismo** (**el egoísmo**).

**The opposite** takes **in-**, **im-** or **ir-**. Before **r** the prefix is **ir-**: **irresponsable**.

**Ser** + adjective equals **tener** + noun: **es valiente** = **tiene valentía**.
b4.e1.texto: His shyness stops him from speaking in public.
b4.e2.texto: My brother is irresponsible and never arrives on time.
b5.f0.texto: My uncle Fermín walks into the restaurant like a captain on his ship.
b5.f1.texto: He is ambitious and persevering, and today he has three restaurants in the city.
b5.f2.texto: His arrogance fills the whole room like smoke from a chimney.
b5.f3.texto: However, he is mean and has never treated anyone to a coffee.
b5.f4.texto: Even his hands seem to be guarding invisible coins.
b5.f5.texto: Eusebio, his brother, lives in a small house with books up to the ceiling.
b5.f6.texto: My mother says with a smile that his generosity has no limits.
b5.f7.texto: My grandmother used to say he had no sense at all because he lent money to anyone.
b5.f8.texto: When someone had to stand up to the owner of the premises, Fermín kept quiet out of sheer cowardice.
b5.f9.texto: Then Eusebio, with his calm manner, took a step forward.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: a tacaño does not want to spend money, not even on a coffee.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Quite the opposite: a generous person gives and shares.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Cobarde is about fear, not about money.
b6.pregunta: What is someone who never treats anyone like?
b7.frase: Su ____ le impide hablar en público.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is the adjective, and after «su» you need a noun.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That word does not exist. The noun of «tímido» ends in «-ez».
b8.frase: Hay que tener valentía para hablar con él
b8.traduccion: You need courage to talk to him
b9.o0.refuerzo: The expression is about the head, not about food.
b9.o1.refuerzo: That is it: it is said fondly, never as an insult.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Terco is obstinate; this expression is about madness.
b9.pregunta: What does «está como una cabra» mean?
b10.frase: Mi hermano es muy ____ y llega tarde.
b10.o0.refuerzo: That word does not exist: before «r» the prefix changes.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That prefix is not used with this word.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: ser + adjective equals tener + noun.
b12.o1.refuerzo: After «tiene» comes a noun, not the adjective.
b12.o2.refuerzo: With that noun the verb is «tener», not «estar».
p.rinde.consejo: «Rendirse» changes «e» to «i»: «me rindo», «se rinde». «No se rinde nunca» means he is persevering.
p.arrogancia.consejo: It comes from «arrogante». The «rr» rolls strongly.
p.anterior.consejo: The opposite is «posterior». It is the same for masculine and feminine.
p.límites.consejo: The accent marks the first syllable: «LÍ-mi-tes». The singular is «límite».
p.irresponsable.consejo: It starts with «ir-» because the base word begins with «r». Same for masculine and feminine.
p.capitán.consejo: The accent is on the last syllable. The plural is «capitanes», with no accent.
p.barco.consejo: It is written with «b». The «b» and «v» sound the same: «vaso», «barco».
p.restaurantes.consejo: Plural of «restaurante». The «au» is a diphthong: «tau».
p.entera.consejo: It is the feminine of «entero» and agrees with «la sala».
p.humo.consejo: The «h» is silent: «U-mo». It comes from a chimney or a fire.
p.chimenea.consejo: It is also the fireplace in the living room, where a fire is lit.
p.guardar.consejo: The «u» is pronounced here because it goes with «a»: «gwar-DAR».
p.invisibles.consejo: Plural of «invisible». It is the same for masculine and feminine. The «v» sounds «b».
p.techo.consejo: The «ch» sounds as in «chocolate». «Bajo el mismo techo» means in the same home.
p.abuela.consejo: It is the feminine of «abuelo». Both together are «los abuelos».
p.prestaba.consejo: It is the imperfect of «prestar»: a repeated action in the past.
p.hubo.consejo: «Hubo que» + infinitive means «it was necessary to». The «h» is silent.
p.enfrentarse.glosa: to face, to stand up to
p.enfrentarse.consejo: It is used with «a»: «enfrentarse a un problema».
p.local.consejo: Here it is a place for a business. As an adjective it means «of the area».
p.callado.consejo: It comes from «callar». The «ll» sounds «y». With «quedarse»: «se quedó callado».
p.pura.consejo: Before a noun it adds force: «pura cobardía» is nothing but cowardice.
p.dio.consejo: Past of «dar». It has no accent because it is a single syllable: «dio».
p.loco.consejo: The feminine is «loca». «Está loco» means he is not thinking straight.
